$comment: The v1.3 line's release-candidate tag for its PARALLEL compat credential window (founder decision 2026-10-08; four stable cells node/bun x turbopack/webpack, vinext Beta and uncredentialed). Independent of .github/compat-credential-ref.json, which pins the v1.0 window: a v1.3 bump restarts only the v1.3 window. Read from main by .github/workflows/compat-credential-v1.3.yml via scripts/compat-credential-line.mjs, which REFUSES a tag not on the v1.3 line. Bumping rcTag requires regenerating that workflow from the new tag in the same PR (docs/RELEASING.md).

publishedBytesBumpMarker.reason: Lead-delegated 2026-10-14 (UTC), the Next.js peer-range and 16.4 ISR-scoping backport to the 1.3 line (#2252, from #2242, #2285 and #2288 on main), applying the same scoped-marker rule as the 1.3.1 PPR backport and the next/image backport. It changes @getknext/core's shipped bytes relative to v1.3.0-rc.10: package.json's next peer range goes from >=16.0.0 to >=16.0.0 <16.5.0; dist/adapters/cache-handler.js withholds a stored ISR window another build wrote on Next 16.4 reads (scopeWindowToBuild); the CLI chunks gain the doctor next-minor row and the next-compat policy module. Like 1.3.0 and 1.3.1, the resulting patch ships decoupled from the credential: the window keeps measuring the rc.10 bytes and no verified claim covers it until a credential cycle runs on it. rcTag is unchanged. Distinct reason from the inherited next/image marker, so the introduced-by-this-PR rule reads it as new.
